messages:
maria: quick sync — thinking about a preview mode for automatic fallback during rollouts. goal: let apps observe fallback behavior (and audit it) before we flip it on for real. idea: an opt-in "preview sandbox" that 1) shows degraded outputs flagged, 2) records full audit stream, 3) doesn't count toward committed capacity billing. thoughts? :thinking_face:
aj: +1 on preview sandbox. couple questions: how do we sample traffic? and how do we prevent the preview from triggering downstream rate limits or quota alarms?
kenji: sample at routing layer with deterministic hashing by request_id/app_id so previews are reproducible. use tiny percent (0.5% by default), plus per-app overrides. prevents noise.
maria: yes deterministic sampling is key. UX needs to surface which requests were sampled and why they fell back (latency/circuit/error). idea for human-readable reason: "latency_p95>250ms" / "model_compat_mismatch" / "quantize_fail".
aj: also need to be careful about token accounting. if preview returns a fallback response we should optionally mark it as "billing:preview" so it doesn't count against free credits or reserved capacity. that avoids surprise chargebacks.
natalie: billing & compliance concern: some customers will insist that preview traffic still flows through their dedicated capacity or VPC. need a toggle: preview in-hosted vs preview-in-dedicated. UX should make that explicit.
ellie: telemetry schema proposal (short): event = fallback.preview.record with fields [request_id, route, fallback_mode, trigger, latency_ms, model_version, kv_cache_hit, sample_bucket, user_reported=false]. retention 90d by default. add a separate audit tape that stores the full input+output for 30d if customer opts in.
kenji: agree on schema. also add a deterministic replay id so we can feed the exact same request into a local replay runner. e.g., replay_id = sha256(request_id + sample_bucket + seed).
maria: UX panel in Console: "Preview traffic" tab that shows a timeline, list of sampled requests, and an "audit" toggle per-request to view full io (if permitted). default: hide PII and show token-level cost estimate.
aj: operationally, we need an escape hatch: if preview causes downstream issues (spam, billing anomalies) we should have a quick kill switch per-customer and global. console button: "Pause previews for this org" + API endpoint.
natalie: and for audits we need a redact workflow. the audit view must have a single-click redact + exportable redaction log for compliance.
ellie: implementation detail: telemetry events must include a consumer-visible tag so customers can filter their dashboards: `preview=true|false`, `preview_sample=0.5%|2%` etc. and we should expose aggregate metrics: fallback_rate_preview, avg_latency_preview_p95.
kenji: on triggers: propose we support multiple trigger types with priorities: 1) explicit policy (rollout step), 2) runtime signals (p95 latency, 5xx spike, model_quality_score drop), 3) circuit-breaker (backend unreachable). Each trigger should attach a confidence score and a TTL. UX should show the active trigger and TTL in the preview timeline.
maria: UX wire: compact row per-sampled-request showing small badges: [fallback_mode: soft|hard], [trigger: latency|error|policy], [audited: Y/N], [replay_id]. clicking expands raw request/response.
natalie: can we unify soft vs hard degrade semantics: soft = return best-effort fallback + mark telemetry; hard = immediate failover to configured fallback model/route and increment fallback budget usage. customers can set which mode is previewable.
aj: note: soft degrade should still enforce safety filters (no PII leakage), and hard degrade must obey quota/billing. important for safety.
maria: question for API design: should preview sampling be set via rollout config or via dedicated Preview API? pros/cons?
kenji: rollout config approach keeps everything in one place and makes preview reproducible across infra. Preview API allows ad-hoc tests but risks divergence. recommend both: default via rollout config + a one-off Preview API for debug sessions (requires org-level permission).
ellie: for audit playback we need deterministic seeds + model version pinning so playback is stable. store model artifacts pointers (model_hash, quant_config) in audit metadata.
natalie: docs ask: how long do we keep previews and audit records? default telemetry 90d, audit full io 30d unless customer buys extended retention. include a retention policy UI.
maria: UX question: how to present preview to product teams without scaring them (they might see degraded answers). propose label with yellow pill: "Preview — may contain degraded fallbacks. Not live." and optional user-facing header for apps (opt-in) so devs can surface to internal testers.
aj: ops checklist: add rate limits for preview replay, backpressure if consumers hit replay API too hard. also add metrics in SLO dashboards: preview_fallback_rate versus live_fallback_rate.
kenji: quick config sketch (YAML):
```
fallback_preview:
  enabled: true
  sample_pct: 0.5
  deterministic_by: request_id
  mode: soft
  triggers:
    - type: latency_p95
      threshold_ms: 250
      ttl_s: 300
    - type: model_quality
      delta_threshold: 0.15
      ttl_s: 600
```
maria: love it. next steps: ellie + kenji to draft telemetry/events + replay_id; aj to spec kill-switch + quota semantics; natalie to write compliance/redaction flow; i'll mock Console wire and copy for PM review. can we aim for a short sync Wed?
ellie: I'll put up a proto event spec in #eng-platform by Tue.
kenji: I'll start a small PoC that samples traffic and writes replay_id to S3 (encrypted). ETA Thu.
aj: I'll prototype the pause-preview API and kill switch demo. ETA Wed EOD.
deploy-bot: deploy 1741113000 started by kenji — preview-poc v0.1 -> staging :rocket:
maria: thanks all. this feels like a clean way to let customers validate fallback behaviors and keep auditability. we'll iterate on UX copy to reduce alarm. :seedling:
